text: A Quaker friend having kindly informed me that I was generally thought proud; that my pride show'd itself frequently in conversation; that I was not content with being in the right when discussing any point, but was overbearing, and rather insolent... I determined endeavouring to cure myself, if I could, of this vice or folly among the rest, and I added Humility to my list.
author: Benjamin Franklin
locator: Chapter IX, Plan for Attaining Moral Perfection
